clue.text: Not being in gear, he can't take off

definitions.text: Not being in gear, he can't take off

parts.words: Not being in gear, he can't take off
parts.note: being in gear reads as a car or machine, but here gear is clothing; someone who never wears any has nothing to remove

explanation.surface: A stalled vehicle or aircraft unable to get airborne because it is out of gear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take off' looks like aircraft or a car pulling away; it means removing clothes, which this person never has on.
explanation.definitionFit: A nudist goes about unclothed, so has no garments to strip away.

clue.text: Apologetic convert

definitions.meaning: the Victorian cardinal who wrote the Apologia Pro Vita Sua defending his change of faith
a convert is someone reborn, a fresh person

explanation.surface: Someone who switched sides and is sorry about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Apologetic' means not sorry but defending a belief: John Henry Newman wrote the Apologia after becoming a Catholic.
explanation.definitionFit: Cardinal John Henry Newman converted from Anglicanism and wrote a celebrated defence of his religious life.

clue.text: Twisters in corrupt trade, and so on

indicators.note: corrupt suggests the letters are spoiled and turned into a different order

explanation.surface: Swindlers operate within a dishonest business and the like.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Corrupt' rearranges TRADE and SO ON; 'in' and 'and' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: Twisters are whirling windstorms, the same violent funnel-shaped storms.

clue.text: Service angle is disreputable

parts.note: the RAF, Royal Air Force, is one of the armed services
to angle is to fish with rod and line

explanation.surface: A serve hit at a sneaky angle in tennis is seen as unsporting.
explanation.definitionFit: Raffish means rakish and slightly dissolute, of doubtful respectability.

clue.text: Eratosthenes' riddle

parts.note: a riddle is a coarse strainer, and the Greek mathematician gave his name to a method for filtering out primes

explanation.surface: A puzzle set by an ancient Greek scholar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Riddle' looks like a puzzle but is a strainer; the method of Eratosthenes finds prime numbers by striking out multiples.
explanation.definitionFit: A riddle is a coarse mesh for separating, and Eratosthenes devised a famous prime-number filtering method.

clue.text: Second characteristic predicament

parts.note: a characteristic is a trait, a distinguishing feature

explanation.surface: A second awkward feature lands someone in a tight spot.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in dire straits means being in serious difficulty, so the word stands for a plight.

clue.text: Occupies a number of social workers

parts.note: ten is a number
ants are social insects, and the worker caste does the labour

explanation.surface: A team of social workers takes over a building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Social workers' looks like care professionals, but ants are social insects with worker castes.
explanation.definitionFit: To tenant a place is to occupy it as a resident, so the verb matches.

clue.text: Alias takes in the Spanish leader of the pack

indicators.note: takes in shows one piece swallowing another, the Spanish word going inside

parts.note: AKA, also known as, introduces an alias
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: Someone using an assumed name welcomes a Spanish wolf-pack chief.
explanation.walkthrough: In the Cub Scouts the adult leader is called Akela, after the wolf in Kipling's Jungle Book.
explanation.definitionFit: Cub Scout packs are led by an adult with this title, from the lead wolf in Kipling.

clue.text: Forcibly removed, quickly went below

definitions.meaning: ripped off a wall or demolished
raced downstairs or downwards in a hurry

explanation.surface: Someone ripped something away and then rushed downstairs.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both demolished or ripped away and rushed downwards.

clue.text: Pub game that not all beer may go with

definitions.text: Pub game that not all beer may go with

parts.words: Pub game that not all beer may go with
parts.note: plays on the saying that life is not all beer and the bowling-style game, so the game partners beer in that phrase

explanation.surface: A tavern pastime that doesn't suit every kind of ale.
explanation.walkthrough: The British saying 'life isn't all beer and ...' means it is not all fun; the game is a bowling one played in pubs.
explanation.definitionFit: Knocking down wooden pins with a ball is a traditional pub game, paired with beer in the saying.

clue.text: Old conflict with odd cause — ultimately shown for weeks in a jar, pickled?

definitions.text: Old conflict with odd cause — ultimately shown for weeks in a jar, pickled?

parts.words: Old conflict with odd cause — ultimately shown for weeks in a jar, pickled?
parts.note: an eighteenth-century Anglo-Spanish war was blamed on a sea captain's severed ear, which he reportedly kept preserved and displayed

explanation.surface: A historical war sparked by something bizarre that ended up pickled in a jar.
explanation.walkthrough: In 1731 Spanish coastguards cut off Captain Robert Jenkins's ear; he later showed it to Parliament, and the Anglo-Spanish war of 1739 took its name from it.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1739 Anglo-Spanish war is named after a mariner whose lopped organ of hearing was its supposed trigger.

clue.text: Miserly obsession with Naval Centre shell prices

indicators.note: the centre of the word naval is its inside, all but its first and last letters
to shell prices is to strip off its outer casing, leaving only the letters within

explanation.surface: A stingy fixation on what the navy pays for its shells.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shell' looks like ammunition the navy buys, but it is a verb: strip the outer letters off prices. 'Centre' does the same job on Naval.
explanation.definitionFit: Greed for money and hoarding it is exactly what a miser is obsessed with.

clue.text: Man's authority can, we hear, reverse many a statute

indicators.note: we hear signals that the word for can is to be taken by its sound, not its spelling

parts.note: a can is a tin

indicators.note: reverse tells us to read the combination of many and a statute backwards

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for 500, a crossword stand-in for many
a statute is a law

explanation.surface: Someone in authority could overturn a heap of laws.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' is the Isle of Man, whose parliament this is; the apostrophe-s makes it look like any man's power.
explanation.definitionFit: The Isle of Man's ancient parliament is the governing body of that island.

clue.text: Provide comprehensive cover for equipment in store

definitions.text: Provide comprehensive cover for equipment in store

parts.words: Provide comprehensive cover for equipment in store
parts.note: comprehensive cover sounds like an insurance policy, but means sealing machinery or ships up against decay while they are laid up unused

explanation.surface: An insurer offering full protection for kit kept in a warehouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Comprehensive cover' is insurance language, but the real cover is a protective coating for laid-up equipment.
explanation.definitionFit: To lay something up in storage and preserve it unused is the sense, from the balls once packed with stored clothes to keep insects away.

clue.text: Stone me! Your old holy man supports leading article

indicators.note: in a down clue the piece that supports the others sits beneath them, so the article goes at the top
the first letter of the word it picks from

parts.note: a is the indefinite article
thy is the old form of your
ST is short for saint

explanation.surface: An exclamation of surprise at an archaic religious figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stone me!' looks like an exclamation, but 'Stone' is the definition and 'me' gives ME. In a down answer 'supports' puts ME THY ST above A, so A comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: A purple quartz is a semi-precious gemstone.

clue.text: Strength one displayed in both partnerships

indicators.note: displayed in tells us one is shown inside the letters for the partnerships

parts.note: in bridge the two partnerships sit South-North and East-West, giving SN and EW
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Unity is shown to be the strength of two business partnerships.
explanation.walkthrough: The partnerships are the two pairs at a bridge table, North-South and East-West.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinews are tendons, and figuratively the word means muscular power or force.

clue.text: Secure records used for treatment at one's fingertips

definitions.text: used for treatment at one's fingertips

parts.note: to nail something is to fasten it securely
files are records

explanation.surface: Locked-away records help treat a condition near at hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At one's fingertips' looks idiomatic, meaning readily available; it is meant literally.
explanation.definitionFit: Emery boards and metal files shape the ends of fingers in a manicure.

clue.text: Vicarious observer to follow leader to the top

indicators.note: in a down answer to the top means the leader is placed above the following piece

parts.note: a guide leads the way
to dog someone is to follow them

explanation.surface: Someone experiencing things second-hand trails a boss upwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vicarious observer' means one who sees on another's behalf: the animal does the seeing for a blind owner.
explanation.definitionFit: This trained animal sees for a blind person, observing on someone else's behalf.

clue.text: Overturn surprising result

definitions.meaning: an unexpected win by an underdog in a contest

explanation.surface: A shock outcome reverses everything.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both knocking a thing over and a sporting shock where the favourite loses.

clue.text: Gifts of old money

definitions.meaning: ancient units of weight and currency, as in the biblical parable

explanation.surface: Presents from inherited wealth.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means natural aptitudes and also ancient weights of silver used as currency.

clue.text: Very happy to refer back, having cast about internally

indicators.note: internally means the rearranged letters go inside the reversed word
back says the word for refer is read in reverse order

parts.note: to refer to something is to cite it

indicators.note: about signals that the letters of cast are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone delighted to look back at the cast that had been shuffled round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' reverses the word for refer, and 'about' shuffles cast; 'internally' places the shuffled letters just after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Ecstasy is overwhelming joy, so being in it is being thrilled.

clue.text: A case for diplomacy?

parts.note: reads as a situation needing tact, but is the official on an embassy staff, who also lends a name to a briefcase

explanation.surface: A situation that calls for tactful handling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Case' looks like a situation; it is a briefcase named after an embassy official.
explanation.definitionFit: An embassy staff member gives a name to the slim document case, so both case and diplomacy point to it.

clue.text: Bishop's given warning about prince

indicators.note: about shows the warning word going round the bishop letter

parts.note: an alert is a warning
B is the chess notation for bishop

explanation.surface: A churchman gives a warning concerning a royal.
explanation.walkthrough: Prince Albert was Queen Victoria's consort.
explanation.definitionFit: Prince Albert, husband of Queen Victoria, is the best-known prince of the name.

clue.text: Philistine collaborator giving head ill-treatment

indicators.note: treatment here means the letters are worked over and reshaped

explanation.surface: A woman who cooperated with the Philistines gave someone's head rough handling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ill-treatment' reads as one word, but 'ill' is fodder and 'treatment' signals rearranging HEAD and ILL. The shearing of Samson's hair is the hidden joke.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Bible she betrayed Samson to the Philistines by having his hair cut.

clue.text: Drinks for audience in the interval

indicators.note: for audience tells us the word for drinks is taken as heard by listeners

parts.note: an animal laps when it drinks

explanation.surface: Refreshments are served to theatre-goers during the interval.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drinks' and 'interval' paint a theatre bar; the answer is a gap of time.
explanation.definitionFit: A lapse of time is a passing period or gap.

clue.text: Miserable mine provided uranium lode, initially

parts.note: a mine is a pit
provided, as in provided that, means if
U is the chemical symbol for uranium

indicators.note: initially means take only the opening letter of lode

explanation.surface: A wretched mine that produced a seam of uranium at first.
explanation.definitionFit: Pitiful and miserable both describe something wretched and deserving sympathy or contempt.

clue.text: Quietly enthusiastic about horse

parts.note: P, piano, is the musical direction for quietly
to be into something is to be keen on it

explanation.surface: Someone is quietly keen on a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: A pinto is a piebald or skewbald horse, a breed with patchy markings.

clue.text: Classical lovers awkwardly hold hands — an epic ballet

indicators.note: awkwardly suggests the letters are clumsily jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: Lovers in a classical tale clumsily hold hands in a grand ballet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Awkwardly' rearranges HOLD HANDS AN EPIC. The pair are the lovers of a Greek pastoral romance, also the title of Ravel's ballet, which 'ballet' points to.
explanation.definitionFit: The shepherd and shepherdess of Longus's Greek romance are a famous classical couple.

clue.text: Rock sounds fine

indicators.note: sounds tells us the synonym for fine is taken by how it is said

parts.note: fine means nice

explanation.surface: Someone approves of a stone's tone.
explanation.definitionFit: A banded metamorphic stone is a common type of crystalline rock.

clue.text: A few are reportedly located in this part of England

parts.note: a few means some

indicators.note: reportedly signals that are is represented by the letter it sounds like

parts.note: are sounds like the letter R
located means set, placed or situated

explanation.surface: A handful of people are said to live in a particular corner of England.
explanation.walkthrough: SOMERSET is a rural county in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a county in the West Country of southwest England.
